sources.entry: Rules for Autocomplete: rough specifications for autocomplete fields

summary.title: Rules for Autocomplete
summary.one_liner: A checklist of ordering, keyboard, and timing rules that make autocomplete fields behave sanely, plus optional features worth considering.
takeaways: Rank exact matches first, then prefix matches, then substring matches, then optionally subsequence and approximate matches.
Sort matches alphabetically and put the shorter option first when one is a prefix of another.
Keep keyboard behavior predictable: Tab accepts the current suggestion, and Enter uses the highlighted selection without reverting to a default.
Aim for results under 100ms, avoid showing stale results after typing stops, and never change a highlighted option when new data loads.
Optional features such as recent-item suggestions, multipart file path matching, and aliases suit some autocomplete contexts but not all.
summary.summary: The author lists rules that autocomplete UIs often break, explaining each with short examples such as typing "Fr" to get "Fresno" before "San Francisco". The rules cover match ordering (exact, prefix, substring, subsequence, approximate), alphabetical sorting, case handling, keyboard behavior for Tab, Enter and the action keys, focus and latency expectations, and stability of highlighted options. A second section describes optional features like showing recent entries, ambiguous-prefix completion, multipart path matching, recursive filtering, spelling correction, aliases, extra result info, context-aware suggestions, and returning to typed text after accepting a suggestion. It is a brief opinionated list rather than an implementation guide.
